verdict.rationale: Lium documents on-demand GPU provisioning from both the CLI (`lium up --gpu H100`) and the API (`POST /executors/rent-by-spec`), plus a console pod-creation flow. It also documents running code on the pod via `lium exec`, Jupyter, or the SDK, so the core of the story is directly supported. However, nothing documents how long it takes from request to running code, so the 'within minutes' part is unproven. Missing for 10: documented or measured provisioning time ('within minutes'), independent or hands-on corroboration of the end-to-end flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision an on-demand GPU instance from the console or API and be running code on it within minutes

citations.quote: pip install lium.io && lium up --gpu H100 --ttl 1h
rent-by-spec (`POST /executors/rent-by-spec`) that rents the cheapest node matching a GPU spec under a `max_price_per_gpu_hour` ceiling
The SDK rents the cheapest matching node, runs the function there, returns the result and removes the pod (or keeps it warm).
Turn it on to get a Jupyter notebook on the pod.
